COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Emerging Technologies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Emerging Technologies.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emerging Technologies.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Emerging Technologies.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Emerging Technologies.

2. When learning Social and Ethical Issues in Networking, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.

3. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

4. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Input Cable Tester
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Information and Communication Technology

5. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

6. When learning Cybersecurity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Cybersecurity.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cybersecurity.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cybersecurity.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cybersecurity.

7. When learning Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.

8. When learning Data Analysis and Visualisation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Analysis and Visualisation.

9. When learning Network Troubleshooting, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Network Troubleshooting.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Troubleshooting.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Troubleshooting.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Troubleshooting.

10. When learning Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.

11. When learning Data Structures, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Data Structures.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Structures.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Structures.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Structures.

12. When learning Robotics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Robotics.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Robotics.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Robotics.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Robotics.

13. When learning Career Opportunities, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Career Opportunities.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Career Opportunities.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Career Opportunities.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Career Opportunities.

14. When learning Cloud Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cloud Computing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Cloud Computing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cloud Computing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cloud Computing.

15. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. Speaker
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

16. When learning Artificial Intelligence Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Concepts.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Network Troubleshooting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Cybersecurity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Cloud Computing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Social and Ethical Issues in Networking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Data Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Web Development II and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
